why_angle: The cited reviews describe the N8's blade disc acting 'like a blower' and the YUKA's brush roller, but none says when the N8's pickup stops working. This page adds Anthbot's own statements that buildup under the deck blocks the airflow and that wet grass is the main cause of clumping, and turns them into a rule: dry grass and a clean deck. It sets this next to the figures with the collector fitted: slope (24° vs 10°), bag size (23 L vs 22 L) and area per charge (about 200 m²).

page.title: Best Robot Lawn Mower with a Bag (2026): Picks Up Clippings and Leaves
page.h1: Best robot lawn mower with a bag
page.desc: Two robot mowers bag clippings in 2026: the ANTHBOT N8 with a built-in 23 L bag and the Mammotion YUKA with an add-on sweeper. Compared on slope, area per charge and the dry-grass rule.
page.answer: Short answer. Yes, there is a robot lawn mower that bags the clippings, and the best in 2026 is the ANTHBOT N8, whose 23 L bag collects grass clippings and leaves. It lifts them only with airflow from its blade disc, so run it on dry grass and clean the deck every week or two.

cells.pickup: Airflow from the blade disc; wet grass or a clogged deck stops it (Anthbot)
Rubber brush roller on the rear sweeper (Notebookcheck)

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Bag size is a tie. 23 L (N8) vs 22 L (YUKA sweeper) is a 1 L difference, about 4%.
  • Slope decides it. With its collector fitted, the N8 is rated for 44.5% (24°) and the YUKA for 18% (10°). 44.5 ÷ 18 ≈ 2.5, so the N8 can bag a slope about 2.5 times as steep.
  • The rated area takes several charges. Notebookcheck measured just under 200 m² per charge with the N8 bagging. 1,500 m² ÷ 200 m² = 7.5 charges to cut the full 0.37 acre once.
  • Time per cut. PCWorld timed 1,200 sq ft in 97 minutes, or 1,200 ÷ 97 × 60 ≈ 740 sq ft an hour. A 5,000 sq ft lawn takes 5,000 ÷ 740 ≈ 6.7 hours of mowing.
  • The collector costs extra on the YUKA. The N8's bag comes in the box. Notebookcheck lists the YUKA sweeper at €699 on its own, so a YUKA 2000 that collects comes to €1,749 + €699 = €2,448 at EU list prices.
  • Noise is a wash. Collecting, the N8 measured 68 dB (PCWorld) and about 70 dB (Notebookcheck). The YUKA with its sweeper measured almost 70 dB (Notebookcheck).
Your lawnBest fit
Up to 0.37 acre, flat or sloped to 24°, and you want the clippings goneANTHBOT N8
Flat (under 18%), up to 0.5 acre, with lots of leaves and twigsMammotion YUKA 2000 + Sweeper Kit
Steep (up to 80%), and fine clippings left on the lawn are acceptableLUBA mini 2 AWD (0.37 acre) or LUBA 2 AWD 3000HX (0.75 acre)

Why the N8 needs dry grass and a clean deck

The N8 has no separate fan or brush. PCWorld describes the blade wings making the airflow so that the disc acts like a blower. Anthbot says that while the N Series mows, a strong airflow lifts and sucks in the clippings and sends them to the rear bag. A radar sensor in the bag detects when it is full and triggers a dump. Notebookcheck saw it empty about every 100 minutes and once at the end of each session.

Because it relies on airflow, the N8 has one weak point, and Anthbot names it: when grass builds up on the underside, it blocks the airflow and clippings drop in thick piles. Anthbot also says wet grass is the primary cause of clumping because it sticks together and to the mower's undercarriage. In practice:

  • Mow dry. Anthbot's test is to walk on the lawn, and if your shoes come away wet, wait. Rain can take hours or even days to drain. The N8's rain sensor pauses it for a preset 3 hours (PCWorld), and that is not the same as a dry lawn.
  • Keep the deck clean. Anthbot's guides say to clear the underside after each mow or every week or two. The N Series blade disc can be rinsed with a garden hose.
  • Plan a place for the dumped clippings. They stay on the lawn. PCWorld lists up to 5 dump areas, each at least 5 × 5 ft, inside the mowing zone.

The YUKA's sweeper picks up mechanically with a rubber brush roller (Notebookcheck), so it does not depend on airflow under the deck. No reviewer has tested either mower collecting on wet grass, so nothing shows the YUKA does better there. {buy:anthbot-n8}

Not recommended

The YUKA with its sweeper on a sloped lawn. The sweeper is what makes the YUKA collect, and it also cuts the slope limit from 45% (24°) to 18% (10°) (Notebookcheck). If any part of your lawn is steeper than 10°, the YUKA can only bag the flat parts, and the N8, rated 24° with its bag on, is the one to buy.
